risks.note: The inability to stay up to date with changing technologies and the latest trends is detrimental to the business. Digitization is emerging as a disruptive force for customers, buyers and technology; combined with changes in delivery models and consumer spending patterns it could threaten growth in traditional IT spending and cause technology obsolescence. The Company must continuously review and upgrade its technology, resources and processes, and relies on strong R&D support from its parent company to stay ahead of the curve.

In a hyper-connected world, cybersecurity incidents that cause economic losses and/or breach company and personal information are a reality for any business. The Company relies on a robust intrusion prevention system and a strong risk management framework, and continuously evaluates the threat landscape.

The IT industry is highly competitive, with competition from local IT companies and MNC IT hardware companies having a sizable presence in low-cost technologies. This can lead to pressure on pricing and vendor consolidation, impacting Company growth and profitability, and new competitors are emerging from adjacent markets and distant geographies.

The functional currency is the Indian Rupee and volatility in exchange movements results in transaction and translation exposure. D-Link has substantial exposure to foreign-exchange risk on account of imports of finished traded products from its parent group companies, and cabling products are subject to fluctuations in raw material prices such as copper. Management predicts the USD position will continue to remain volatile; the Company follows a well-established hedging policy and does not undertake speculative hedging.

Supply chain volatility is a complex and ever-changing challenge. Global semiconductor supply chains were severely affected after the pandemic and faced further disruptions due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict; any sudden disruption of global and domestic supply chains poses a risk for the Company.
